questions.q: What is the core problem this lesson's runbook solves, that Lessons 45 and 46 alone didn't?
options: Lessons 45 and 46 used incorrect commands that the runbook corrects
The knowledge of how to run each failover correctly lived only in whoever performed the test — the runbook makes it usable by someone else, under pressure, without that context
AG_Bellhaven doesn't actually work until a runbook is written
Runbooks are only needed for HA events, never for DR events
questions.explain: A runbook exists so an on-call responder who wasn't part of building or testing the AG can still execute the right procedure correctly.

questions.q: What is the first job of Bellhaven's runbook, before any failover command runs?
options: Routing the incident through a decision tree to determine which procedure — if any — actually applies
Immediately running FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS regardless of the situation
Notifying customers before confirming anything internally
Restoring the nightly full backup from Lesson 43
questions.explain: The decision tree comes first, distinguishing a non-event, a local failure (Procedure A), and a site disaster (Procedure B) before any command is run.

questions.q: Why does the runbook require IT Director escalation before Procedure B but not Procedure A?
options: Procedure B accepts possible data loss via FORCE_FAILOVER_ALLOW_DATA_LOSS and should never be a single person's decision under pressure, while Procedure A is a safe, no-data-loss operation
Escalation is only a formality with no operational purpose
Procedure A requires more technical skill than Procedure B
IT Director approval is required by SQL Server itself before running any ALTER AVAILABILITY GROUP command
questions.explain: The escalation gate exists specifically because Procedure B accepts a real risk of data loss — a second person should confirm the scope of the outage first.

questions.q: What does the runbook's verification checklist include specifically for Procedure B that Procedure A doesn't need?
options: Disabling the Availability Group permanently
Measuring and logging the actual data-loss window before declaring recovery complete
Re-creating the listener BHFS-AGL from scratch
Restarting the SQL Server service on all three replicas
questions.explain: Because Procedure B may have lost data, the runbook requires measuring that gap (as covered in Lesson 46) as part of verification — Procedure A has no data loss to measure.

questions.q: What does 'rollback' mean for Procedure A, and why doesn't Procedure B have an equivalent simple rollback?
options: Rollback for Procedure B means undoing the forced failover automatically once Columbus comes back online
Both procedures roll back identically by restoring the nightly full backup
Neither procedure has any rollback process defined

Procedure A's rollback is just re-running FAILOVER back to the original primary once the cause is fixed; Procedure B instead requires rejoining the old replicas as new secondaries, not reverting anything
questions.explain: A synchronous pair's failover is symmetric and reversible; a forced failover to the DR replica breaks the original relationship and requires rejoining, not a simple reversal.
